task_instance: Queue a Wispr Flow dictation correction and batch-apply it to the Wispr Flow dictionary database, i.e. run the bundled wispr-fix.sh script: `add "Clauthe Code" "Codex"` then `dry-run`/`flush` so the correction really lands in the Wispr Flow SQLite dictionary (the skill's core stated deliverable).
blocker_detail: The skill is a macOS-only automation wrapper around the proprietary Wispr Flow desktop dictation application, and this runtime is Linux (uname: Linux x86_64). Every command in the bundled script first runs check_deps(), which hard-requires the sqlite3 CLI (absent here), the jq CLI (present), and a separate helper script wispr_dictionary.py belonging to a different skill (wispr-analytics) that is not bundled with this skill and is absent on disk. The actual core deliverable (the flush command) additionally needs: the Wispr Flow GUI application itself; the macOS-only commands osascript, say and the mac flavor of open -a used to quit and relaunch that app; and the live Wispr Flow SQLite database under the mac Application Support folder (absent) that the corrections are written into. None of these are provided by, or installable into, this Linux developer runtime (Wispr Flow is a closed-source macOS GUI app, not a package-manager dependency). So even the minimal queue step could not run, and the batch-apply step is impossible. A separate obstacle also appeared: the auto-mode safety classifier refused to execute the copied external script (reason 'Code from External'), but the runtime/platform mismatch above is the fundamental, independent blocker.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and scripts/wispr-fix.sh from the skill repo (only those two files exist under the skill root: SKILL.md and scripts/wispr-fix.sh). Script hardcodes DB_PATH to the mac Application Support Wispr Flow flow.sqlite, DICT_SCRIPT to ~/.claude/skills/wispr-analytics/scripts/wispr_dictionary.py, and uses osascript/say/open -a plus pgrep 'Wispr Flow' for lifecycle. Dependency probe in work dir: `jq --version`=jq-1.7 (present); `sqlite3 --version`=MISSING; `python3`=3.13 (present); `osascript`=MISSING; `say`=MISSING; `open`=/usr/bin/open (Linux variant, not mac app launcher); DICT_SCRIPT path -> 'No such file or directory'; Wispr Flow flow.sqlite -> 'No such file or directory'; uname -> Linux ... x86_64. Attempts to run `wispr-fix.sh add` and `bash wispr-fix.sh add` were denied by the auto-mode classifier ('Code from External'). Copied script to work dir at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r174/wispr-fix.sh. No deliverable produced; core intent (corrections applied to a running Wispr Flow dictionary) cannot be realized on this Linux runtime.
